rationale: The request combines a reported broken release pipeline with additive support for Python 3.14 and Windows, so the plan investigates current packaging contracts and existing cross-platform build patterns.

queries.intent: Locate Navigator packaging metadata and compiled-extension declarations.
Locate all Navigator release and package-build workflows.
Read Navigator packaging metadata to identify Python classifiers, build backend, package discovery, and wheel tags.
Read the setup extension declarations and manifest rules that determine Cython contents in distributions.
Read the release workflow build matrix, cibuildwheel configuration, artifact collection, and publication paths.
Find Cython, Rust, cibuildwheel, platform, and Python-version references while excluding the virtual environment.
Inspect recent build-related history and the latest Cython wheel fix for regressions and constraints.
Read the asyncdb release workflow as the requested local comparison for cross-platform wheel production.
Read asyncdb setup metadata and extension declarations to compare mixed Cython/native build contracts.
Read asyncdb portability task contracts for Windows tags, compiled extension checks, and smoke-test boundaries.
Check whether a local Rust source tree or Cargo manifest exists in Navigator itself.
Attempt a local wheel build to identify environment or packaging failures that CI may reproduce.

expected_findings: Navigator currently has Cython extension declarations and no local Rust/Cargo build manifest.
Navigator release CI is Linux-focused and publication filters only manylinux wheels.
Navigator metadata contains stale or contradictory wheel/platform declarations.
asyncdb provides an explicit cp310-cp314, Windows AMD64, archive-validation pattern.
The linked Actions failure cannot be independently inspected from this environment.
